---
title: "Lessons from quantitative easing in the United States: A guide for Australian policymakers"
date: "2019-06-18"
categories: ["Economics", "Monetary Policy"]
---

I have a new report out with the United States Studies Centre on [Lessons from Quantitative Easing in the United States: A Guide for Australian Policymakers](https://www.ussc.edu.au/analysis/lessons-from-quantitative-easing-in-the-united-states-a-guide-for-australian-policymakers). It argues that the RBA could implement a smaller but more effective program of asset purchases by learning from the US Fed’s missteps.

There is a write up by John Kehoe in the [AFR](https://www.afr.com/news/economy/rba-bond-buying-more-potent-in-australia-20190614-p51xtu). There is also an op-ed version in [The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/below-zero-is-reverse-how-the-reserve-bank-would-make-quantitative-easing-work-118843).

In this piece in [The Mandarin](https://www.themandarin.com.au/110122-quantitative-easing-does-not-increase-inequality/), I explain why Tim Wilson MP and others are mistaken in their criticisms of QE. Opposing QE when it is needed will lead to more of the interventions Tim otherwise opposes.

Bloomberg’s Michael Heath also [quotes](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/news/australia-finally-debating-qe-even-140000833.html) from my report.
